# F7: mirror-twin neurons and layer-0 filters (visuals)

Generated by `scripts/f7_visuals.py` on 2026-11-09 23:57, commit aeb57bed18. Model `tiny`; fit run `tiny_out/runs\f7\tiny_fit\results\e1_operators.npz` (fit seed 0, SHA-256 5900d1632802); seed 0. TINY MODE: random tiny ViT and synthetic images, not a result.
Visualisation set: 40 synthetic images from the k-NN bank rows (disjoint from the fit images) (640 patch tokens per block). Every number below is read from the CSV files in this folder.

## Result in brief

- Chosen pairs: 24 (block 1: 8, block 2: 8, block 4: 8).
- Twin correlation (mean of both directions) over the chosen pairs: min -0.01, median 0.07, max 0.13. Random-partner control: min -0.06, median -0.01, max 0.06.
- In 0 of 24 chosen pairs the twin is the best-correlated partner of both neurons among all 256 neurons of the block.
- On each neuron's own top patches, the twin's activation on the mirrored image at the mirrored position is on average 0.10 of the neuron's activation (random partner 0.05).
- Layer 0: the even subspace of A_0 holds 0.52 of the (channel-centred) patch-embedding energy and its filters are 0.58 symmetric by energy; the odd subspace holds 0.48 and is 0.41 symmetric (all filters together: 0.50). With a random involution of the same d+ the two subspaces are 0.51 and 0.49 symmetric.

## Layer 0

- A_0: d+ = 34, d- = 30. Median over rows of the largest squared entry: 0.106 (1 for a permutation), so A_0 is dense in the channel basis and channels are not paired one to one; the filters are shown along principal directions of the even and odd subspaces instead.
- Breaking share of the patch embedding, ||W - W_eq||^2 / ||W||^2 with W_eq = (W + A_0 W F) / 2: 0.417 (random involution with the same d+: 0.493).
- even subspace (dimension 34): energy share 0.52, symmetric-energy fraction 0.58; first principal filters: 0.57, 0.59, 0.54, 0.58, 0.59, 0.54, 0.60, 0.58.
- odd subspace (dimension 30): energy share 0.48, symmetric-energy fraction 0.41; first principal filters: 0.40, 0.41, 0.40, 0.43, 0.40, 0.46, 0.41, 0.40.

## Definitions

- Twin pairing and scores: from the fit run (run_e1.py): S = (R + R^T) / 2, R[i, j] = corr(zt_i, z_j) over all tokens (CLS, registers and patches) of the fit images, z = fc1 pre-activation, zt = the same on the mirrored image un-flipped. Matching weight w_uv = 2 S_uv - S_uu - S_vv. Pairs ranked by w (ties: S_uv, then u).
- Twin r of a pair (u, v): corr(v on the mirrored image at the mirrored position, u on the original) and the same with u and v swapped, averaged; post-GELU activations, patch tokens only, all patches of the visualisation set (float64 sums). It is 1 for an exactly equivariant block.
- Random r: the same with a random partner rho(u) that is neither u nor v (seed 0 * 1000 + block), for each neuron of the pair; one random partner per neuron.
- Top patches: the images with the largest activation of the neuron at any patch, at most one patch per image; crops show the 3 x 3 patch neighbourhood (grey outside the image), the outlined square is the patch itself.
- Layer-0 filters: W = patch-embedding kernels as a d x (3 p p) matrix, centred over channels. Principal filters of a parity subspace: right singular vectors of V^T W (V an orthonormal basis of the subspace); energy share s_k^2 / ||W||^2; symmetric-energy fraction ||(g + flip g) / 2||^2 / ||g||^2 (flip = left-right mirror of the kernel); for a whole subspace the same ratio for V^T W. Filters are drawn as 0.5 + 0.5 g / max|g| in the (normalised) input colour channels.

[Check on the figure before keeping this sentence: the twin's patches look like mirror images of the neuron's.] Numbers: correlation between the twin's activation on the mirrored image and the neuron's own activation over all patches (in brackets: a random partner). (b) Patch-embedding filters along the principal directions of the even (A_0 = +1) and odd (A_0 = -1) subspaces of the layer-0 mirror operator; numbers: symmetric-energy fraction. (c) Over every twin pair of each block: median (marker) and 10th to 90th percentile (bar) of the twin correlation and of the random-partner control.
- figF7_twins_full: all 24 chosen pairs, top 6 patches of each neuron.
- figF7_layer0_filters: (a) the first principal filters of each parity; (b) symmetric-energy fraction of every principal filter against its energy share, for A_0 and for a random involution.

## Caveats

- The figure is qualitative; the correlations above are the evidence. The pairing was fitted on pre-activations over all tokens of the fit images; the check uses post-GELU patch tokens of other train images, so it is a held-out check of the same pairing.
- The twin's top patches are searched independently over the original images; they are not the mirrored crops of the neuron's patches.
- The forward pass runs in full precision.
- One fit seed (the fit run's); the random-partner control uses one random partner per neuron.
